name: grill-with-docs
description: Grill a plan against the domain model. Sharpen terminology, update GLOSSARY.md and ADRs as decisions crystallize.

steps.name: Scan documentation
steps.instruction: Check what documentation structure exists. Read the project's CLAUDE.md for the full layout. Scan for: GLOSSARY.md (or GLOSSARY-MAP.md), docs/adr/ or docs/decisions/, SCOPE.md, CONVENTIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, TESTING.md, architecture rule catalogue (architecture-rule-catalogue.md or similar), endpoint registries (contracts/*-endpoints.json). Create files lazily - only when you have something to write.

steps.name: Catalogue-driven grill
steps.instruction: If an architecture rule catalogue exists, follow reference/catalogue-grill.md: initialize a per-family checklist, grill each family systematically (one at a time, depth-first). Produce consolidated decision-tree ADRs (one per root question with branching sub-decisions), not granular per-decision docs. Target 6-8 ADRs for complex projects. Cross-reference against the catalogue's open items. Check SCOPE.md and endpoint registries before recommending any changes - never cut features or endpoints without explicit user approval.

steps.name: Interview
steps.instruction: Interview relentlessly about every aspect of the plan. One question at a time, waiting for feedback before continuing. For each question, provide a recommended answer. If a question can be answered by exploring the codebase, explore instead of asking. Challenge against the glossary: when a term conflicts with GLOSSARY.md, call it out immediately. Sharpen fuzzy language: propose precise canonical terms for vague or overloaded words. Discuss concrete scenarios that probe edge cases. Cross-reference with code: if the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees.
checklist: Vague terms sharpened to canonical names
Architecture questions grilled against constraint sheet dimensions (workload, state, trust, operations)

steps.name: Update docs inline
steps.instruction: Update GLOSSARY.md inline when a term is resolved - don't batch. GLOSSARY.md must be devoid of implementation details; it is a glossary and nothing else. Cascade to other project docs when decisions affect them: naming pattern -> conventions/NAMING.md, scope change -> SCOPE.md, dependency change -> ARCHITECTURE.md, test expectations -> TESTING.md. Only cascade when the doc exists and the change is genuine.
checklist: Resolved terms written to GLOSSARY.md immediately
Cascades applied to affected existing docs
No docs created just to cascade into

steps.name: Offer ADRs sparingly
steps.instruction: Only offer an ADR when all three hold: (1) hard to reverse - cost of changing later is meaningful, (2) surprising without context - future reader will wonder why, (3) result of a real trade-off - genuine alternatives existed. If any is missing, skip the ADR. Consolidate related decisions into a single ADR. Each answers a root question with branching sub-decisions. When an ADR passes the three-gate test, structure it using the constraint sheet: record workload assumptions, state ownership, trust boundaries, operations plan, one rejected alternative with revisit trigger.
checklist: Three-gate test applied to every ADR candidate
Related decisions consolidated into single ADRs
ADRs include constraint sheet dimensions and revisit trigger

tone: Adversarial but constructive - stress the plan against the domain model.
